documents.title: Repository AI context
documents.description: The protocol of the layer: what it holds, who owns which half, how it is discovered, and what outranks what.

documents.title: Tracked repository context
documents.description: The tracked half of the layer and what each section under it is for.

documents.title: Published releases
documents.description: One record per published release, written by the release pipeline and read by every projection of the public release metadata.

documents.title: Architecture decisions
documents.description: Accepted, durable decisions about how this repository is built.

documents.title: Applications
documents.description: The contexts the tool suits, when each fits and when it does not, composed from use cases.

documents.title: Automation inventory
documents.description: Every unit of this repository's automation, its migration disposition, and the exemption that allows a shell unit to remain shell.

documents.title: Benchmarks
documents.description: The recorded baselines a performance claim is compared against, one directory per measured surface.

documents.title: Continuous integration
documents.description: The gates this repository runs, which changed paths select them, and what publication may spend.

documents.title: Deployments
documents.description: One canonical object per deployment of this repository's executable; every container and provider artifact is generated from it and none of them is authoritative.

documents.title: Evidence
documents.description: The recorded executions a claim's proof is read from — what ran, against which commit, and with what result.

documents.title: Product features
documents.description: What the product does for a person, one feature per file, each made of things the other registries already own; every surface that presents a feature is derived from these files.

documents.title: Knowledge
documents.description: How repository knowledge is declared and discovered, never collected.

documents.title: Mesh
documents.description: One canonical object that says whether this repository's servers participate in mesh discovery, over which transports, and whom they trust; absent or disabled means no socket opens.

documents.title: Profiles
documents.description: How much context, effort and ceremony a task gets, declared per working mode.

documents.title: Project model
documents.description: Milestones as outcomes, issues as execution contracts, and a dependency graph that decides what is next.

documents.title: Prompt assets
documents.description: The provider-neutral prompts the tool renders, with the tokens it fills in.

documents.title: Provider templates
documents.description: The one source each provider bootstrap is rendered from; the files at the root are output.

documents.title: Repository rules
documents.description: The rule object format, where rules live, how they are loaded and composed.

documents.title: Session records
documents.description: One immutable record per closed execution episode, derived from git and the ledger and shared with every surface.

documents.title: Skills
documents.description: Reusable provider-neutral operational procedures, loaded only when the task is about them.

documents.title: Use cases
documents.description: The tasks people perform with the tool, each one a file with the commands, rules and claims it names and the scenario section that proves it.

documents.title: Why this tool exists
documents.description: The operational moments this tool answers, the audiences that recognise them and the areas they fall under, each one a file that every projection is derived from.

documents.title: Workflows
documents.description: The multi-step processes a worker follows here, and when each applies.

documents.title: External workspaces
documents.description: One declaration per external workspace this repository is authorised to read; the content it names is this checkout's state and is never here.

documents.title: Token economics benchmark
documents.description: The methodology, suites and task corpus that measure what a session consumes with Majordomus and without it, and the raw runs recorded under them.

documents.title: Publication baselines
documents.description: What publishing the site cost on a named platform, kept as the comparison for the next run.

documents.title: Executable baselines
documents.description: Per-platform baselines for the Rust executable's commands, with the policy that decides a regression.

documents.title: Candidate records
documents.description: What the tool derived from the ledger and git at an episode boundary and nobody has reviewed yet, discovered as a knowledge source class.

documents.title: Curated notes
documents.description: What this repository chose to write about itself, discovered as a knowledge source class.

documents.title: Plan critiques
documents.description: The adversarial pass over an intent's plan, as structured findings with their resolutions.

documents.title: Gap analyses
documents.description: What a worker observed of this repository against an intent's criteria, at one commit.

documents.title: Intents
documents.description: What must become true above the milestones that realise it, with the evidence that settles it.

documents.title: Issues
documents.description: Execution contracts: one bounded change each, with its scope, its dependencies and the evidence it must leave.

documents.title: Milestones
documents.description: One outcome each, written as the problem it ends and the state that proves it ended.

documents.title: Project rules
documents.description: The rules this repository wrote for itself, one file each, resolved with the vendored baseline.

documents.title: Product domains
documents.description: The few things the product controls, one domain per file; every feature names exactly one, and each domain's members, interfaces and evidence are derived from the features that name it.
